result.summary: Restricts wallet transaction rebroadcasting so transactions are only relayed to peers if they were not already present in the local mempool. Adds a broadcast mode in node transaction submission to relay only upon successful mempool addition, and updates wallet rebroadcast functional tests to verify the behavior.
result.problem: Periodic wallet rebroadcasts unconditionally relay unconfirmed transactions to peers that have not yet seen an inv for them. When a transaction is already present in mempools across the network, this redundant relay leaks privacy by associating the broadcasting node with ownership of the transaction.
evidence: Addresses privacy leak identified in #36403 ('Rethinking Transaction Rebroadcasting'): 'While this is broadcast is limited to peers that have not previously been inv'd the transaction, there is still a privacy leak in this double relay of a transaction, especially so for transactions that are still in nodes' mempools.'
result.scope_notes: Diff is omitted from context, but commit messages indicate changes to node transaction broadcast interfaces, wallet resubmission logic, and test harness refactoring.
result.card: Restricts wallet transaction rebroadcasting to only relay transactions to peers if they had dropped out of and were successfully re-added to the local mempool. Previously, unconfirmed transactions were unconditionally rebroadcast to new peers even if they remained in the mempool, causing a privacy leak that signaled transaction ownership to peers. Addresses issues raised in issue #36403 regarding transaction rebroadcast privacy leaks.

risk.why: A flaw in the rebroadcast filter could suppress relaying stuck transactions to peers when needed, leaving user transactions unconfirmed indefinitely.
